title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: Σ = P^1(C), the Riemann sphere. J (or I) = {R_i} is a set of three marked points, presumably 0, 1, ∞. Σ* = Σ \ J. On the previous page Grothendieck forms the real blow-up Σ' of Σ at the R_i, whose exceptional curves are the real projective lines P(T_{Σ,R_i}). He then cuts Σ' along these circles to get a compact surface with boundary Σ̃. This is the oriented real blow-up, a pair of pants. Its boundary is ∐ U_i, where U_i = (T_{Σ,R_i} \ 0)/R_{>0} is the circle of tangent directions at R_i.

This page states three facts and a heuristic.

(13) Restriction gives functors Rev(Σ̃) → Rev(Σ̃^0) → Rev(Σ*), where Σ̃^0 = Σ̃ \ ∂Σ̃ = Σ̃|Σ*. The first is an equivalence of categories of (étale/topological) coverings, because a boundary collar retracts. The second is an isomorphism, induced by the homeomorphism Σ̃^0 ≅ Σ*.

(14) Hence there is an equivalence of fundamental groupoids 'in the broad sense', Π_1(Σ̃) → Π_1(Σ*). Here the base 'points' may be more general objects, apparently simply connected pieces or universal-cover-type fibre functors.

(15) Composing with the maps induced by U_i ⊂ Σ̃ gives Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ*). This embeds the 'boundary circle' groupoids into the fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere. Each such map yields a family of tangential base points at the puncture R_i (one for each tangent direction), together with the local loop, i.e. the inertia/cusp generator.

Heuristic. Picture Σ̃ as drawn inside Σ*: remove from Σ* the interiors of fictitious 'infinitely small' discs D_i. These are identified with the unit discs of T_{Σ,R_i}, or with the cones on the U_i. Then read (14) as coming from this fictitious inclusion.

The next page explains the purpose. One works with elements of Π_1(Σ̃) based at points of Σ*, at points of the boundary circles, or at 1-connected subsets of Σ̃ that 'overflow' naturally into the boundary. A group Γ acts by transport of structure on (Σ, J) and hence on (14) and (15); this is presumably the symmetry group S_3 of {0,1,∞}, possibly with complex conjugation. Notation must be kept invariant under this action.

The overall goal is a canonical, symmetry-equivariant combinatorial description of π_1 / the fundamental groupoid of P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, with base points at the cusps. This is the basic object for the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower in genus 0.
errors: No genuine error on this page. In (13) the first functor is an equivalence only; the second is a strict isomorphism of categories, induced by a homeomorphism. Grothendieck labels them correctly.

Previous page (context): the non-orientable surface Σ' (sphere with three discs replaced by Möbius bands) has χ = -1. Writing χ = 1 - g with g = 2 is not the standard convention. For non-orientable surfaces χ = 2 - k, so Σ' is the connected sum of 3 real projective planes (non-orientable genus 3). Grothendieck's 'genus 2' is at best a non-standard convention (e.g. the genus of the orientation double cover would be 2, since its χ is -2).

ideas.what: Oriented real blow-up of a punctured Riemann surface at its punctures: a compact surface with boundary whose interior is Σ* and whose boundary circles are the circles of tangent directions at the punctures.
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama log space; bordification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (A'Campo for the real oriented blow-up; Kato–Nakayama 1999 in log geometry)

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid 'au sens large', whose base objects include boundary points of the blow-up, i.e. tangent directions at punctures, and simply connected subsets rather than only points.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points; fundamental groupoid with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points' (1989, §15); also Ihara, Anderson
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses Teichmüller groupoids with carefully chosen base points. Whether tangential base points are explicitly there is unsure.

ideas.what: The maps Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ*) induced by the boundary circles, giving the cusp (inertia) subgroupoids with canonical tangential bases.
ideas.modern_name: inertia/cusp subgroups at tangential base points; local monodromy

ideas.what: The heuristic of 'infinitely small' fictitious discs removed around the punctures, identified with unit tangent discs, so that Σ̃ is pictured inside Σ*.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point as an infinitesimal neighbourhood of the puncture

ideas.what: Insistence that all constructions and notations be equivariant for the symmetry group Γ acting on (P^1, {0,1,∞}).
ideas.modern_name: S_3- (and complex conjugation-) equivariant presentation of π_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}); relates to the hexagon/2-cycle relations of GT

missed.claim: Historical priority detail. In notes from ca. 1978–81, Grothendieck already uses the oriented real blow-up of P^1 at 0, 1, ∞ to define a fundamental groupoid whose base 'points' include tangent directions at the cusps. This is in effect tangential base points, a decade before Deligne's 1989 formalisation. The mathematics itself is standard today.
missed.quote: "dessinant" Σ̃ sur Σ*, comme une région qui serait contenue dans Σ* en lui enlevant l'intérieur de disques fictifs D_i "infiniment petits", qui s'identifient aux disques unités des T_{Σ,R_i}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the tangential-base-point viewpoint for the Galois action on π_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}) was part of Grothendieck's own programme before the Esquisse. This is relevant to attributing the origins of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard: oriented real blow-up, tangential base points, cusp inertia. Its interest is historical. It shows Grothendieck setting up tangential base points via the real blow-up, in an explicitly symmetry-equivariant way, apparently years before Deligne 1989. That is a moderately notable unpublished detail, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: (13): the source category is Rev(Σ̃) and the labels are 'équiv' under the first arrow and 'iso' under the second. The machine transcription is correct here. 'Rev et' should be read as 'Rev ét' (revêtements étales) or 'Rev top'.

The parenthetical after 'groupoïdes fondamentaux au sens large' is more plausibly '(cf. et leurs objets ... les revêtements 1-connexes)' rather than 'les sept[?]'. It indicates that the base objects are (pointings of) 1-connected coverings.

The crossed-out '[-trois-]' before 'disques' and the inserted 'l'intérieur de' and 'fictifs' are correctly placed. The margin note reads roughly: 'plus précisément au lieu de travailler sur Σ* ... travailler sur Σ̃'.
In (15) the crossed-out symbol before U_i is a struck-through Σ. The intended term is Π_1(U_i), with U_i the boundary circles. The next page writes V_i, likely the same objects.
